    AI Overview
    Cori Close is the highly successful head coach of UCLA women’s basketball (since 2011), known for building a top-tier program and leading the Bruins to their first Final Four and a Big Ten Tournament title in the 2024-25 season. A 2025 National Coach of the Year, she has over 300 wins at UCLA. 
    Key Highlights & Career 
    • UCLA Tenure: As of April 2026, Close is the winningest coach in UCLA women’s basketball history, surpassing 300 victories.
    • 2024-25 Success: She led the team to a historic Final Four appearance and swept major National Coach of the Year awards (AP, Naismith, USBWA, WBCA).
    • Coaching Style: Recognized for building strong relationships, combining discipline with care, and emphasizing player development over just wins.
    • USA Basketball: Served as head coach for the 2021 FIBA U19 World Cup gold-medal team and assistant for the 2019 U19 and 2018 U18 gold-medal squads.
    • Background: Played at UC Santa Barbara (team captain 1992, 1993) and served as associate head coach at Florida State for seven seasons. 
    Personal Life 
    • "Mother Bruin": Her mother, Patti Close, is a staple at games, nicknamed "Mother Bruin" by the team.
    • Coaching Philosophy: Frequently speaks on the challenges of balancing intense coaching demands, NIL, and the transfer portal, but remains dedicated to her players. 
    Close has been recognized as a premier recruiter and mentor, establishing UCLA as a consistent national powerhouse.
